factors.name: Variant variability and entropy
factors.summary: Normalized EPA sequence entropies, entropy measures, heterogeneity_rate_variants and n_variants load around 0.85–0.95. The ratio_top_*_variants measures, std_variant_occurrence and ratio_most_common_variant load negatively (-0.78 to -0.93), so the factor contrasts logs spread over many distinct variants with logs dominated by a few frequent variants. It is the largest factor (27.8% of variance), and several trace-length and DFG measures cross-load on it at 0.5–0.75.

factors.name: Event volume and activity frequency
factors.summary: Activity occurrence statistics (0.78–0.91), the non-normalized EPA entropies (about 0.78–0.82), n_events, average_edit_distance and central trace-length measures (0.68–0.75) load here, and event_density loads negatively (-0.69). Together they describe how many events a log has and how often its activities occur, which is a size notion. Many of these measures cross-load on Factor 1 or Factor 3, and n_events, epa_sequence_entropy and average_edit_distance sit at the communality bound.

factors.name: Activity alphabet and trace-length dispersion
factors.summary: n_unique_activities and distinct-activities measures load above 0.9, together with trace-length dispersion measures (geometric_std, coefficient_variation, iqr, std at 0.73–0.83), advanced_trace_diversity and number_of_ties. trace_len_entropy, epa_normalized_variant_entropy and density_dfg load negatively. Logs with many activities and heterogeneous trace lengths therefore have sparser directly-follows graphs. The factor mixes two notions, alphabet size and length spread, and several trace-length measures cross-load with Factor 2.

factors.name: Concentration of start and end activities
factors.summary: Location statistics of start activities load at 0.94–0.98 and those of end activities at 0.79–0.88. The counts of unique start and end activities and start_activities_std load negatively (about -0.78 to -0.80). The factor therefore separates logs with one or few entry and exit activities from logs with many. n_cut_vertices_dfg and separability_ratio_dfg (0.86–0.88) load on it as well, which suggests that such logs have DFGs with more cut vertices.

factors.name: DFG edge count and connectivity
factors.summary: Five measures of the number and connectivity of directly-follows edges load moderately (0.59–0.66). All five cross-load on Factor 1 at 0.52–0.55, so this factor is only partly separate from variant variability. The factor explains 3.6% of the variance, and several of these measures are linearly dependent.

factors.name: Loops within traces
factors.summary: All loop measures of the Repetitions group load here (0.60–0.88) with no strong cross-loadings, so the factor clearly captures how often and how large loops occur. It explains 3.1% of the variance. n_traces_with_repetition does not join it and loads mainly on Factor 2.

factors.name: Dominant start activity frequency
factors.summary: The factor is carried by start_activities_max (0.66) and secondarily by start_activities_variance (0.59) and start_activities_std (0.49). start_activities_variance cross-loads almost equally and with opposite sign on Factor 4 (-0.62). It is a weak factor with 2.0% of the variance.

factors.name: Spread of end activity frequencies
factors.summary: Only end_activities_std (0.81) and end_activities_variance (0.78) load clearly, and both also load moderately negatively on Factor 4. The factor rests on two closely related measures and explains 1.7% of the variance.

factors.name: Residual trace-length histogram (weak)
factors.summary: No measure is assigned to this factor. Its highest loadings are trace_len_hist9 (0.55), trace_len_hist5 (0.42), eventropy_lempel_ziv_flattened (0.38) and trace_len_hist8 (0.34), and these histogram bins are unassigned because of low communality. The factor is too weak to interpret reliably.

factors.name: Shape of activity frequency distribution
factors.summary: activities_kurtosis (0.74) and activities_skewness (0.62) define the factor, so it reflects how unevenly occurrences are distributed over activities. activities_skewness also loads -0.50 on Factor 1. Only two measures carry it, with 1.5% of the variance.

factors.name: Trace-length histogram bins 4 and 7
factors.summary: Two individual trace-length histogram bins load strongly (0.84–0.87) and nothing else does. This is a narrow, measure-specific factor and has no general meaning.

factors.name: Trace-length histogram bins 1 and 10
factors.summary: trace_len_hist1 (0.87) and trace_len_hist10 (0.77) form this factor, which may relate to the extreme bins of the length distribution. It rests on two histogram bins only.

factors.name: Frequency of rare activities
factors.summary: activities_min (0.53) is the only assigned measure, supported by activities_q1 (0.42) and activities_median (0.30). The factor seems to capture how often the least frequent activities occur. Its loadings are moderate and the factor is weak.

factors.name: Shape of trace-length histogram
factors.summary: trace_len_kurtosis_hist (0.69) and trace_len_skewness_hist (0.66) load here, with trace_len_hist6 at 0.44. Both shape measures also load about 0.5–0.55 on Factor 3. The factor describes the shape of the length distribution beyond its spread.

factors.name: Residual factor (uninterpretable)
factors.summary: No measure is assigned to this factor, and its largest loadings are only about 0.25–0.31 in absolute value (mean_variant_occurrence -0.31, end_activities_q3 0.30). With 1.0% of the variance it should not be interpreted.

interpretation.overall: Bartlett's test is significant and the overall KMO of 0.88 is well above 0.6, so the data are suitable for factor analysis. The 15 varimax factors explain 89% of the variance, but four factors dominate (about 69% together): variant variability and entropy, event volume and activity frequency, activity alphabet and trace-length dispersion, and concentration of start and end activities. Two further factors are clear but small: DFG connectivity, which is substantially cross-loaded with Factor 1, and loops within traces. Factors 7–15 are each carried by one or two measures, often single trace-length histogram bins, or by no assigned measure at all. They look like measure-specific rather than substantive dimensions. Six trace_len_hist bins are unassigned for low communality, and end_activities_max and cyclicity_dfg are unassigned for low loadings.
caveats: The correlation matrix is singular because of linear dependencies (e.g. n_edges_dfg, number_of_successions, cyclomatic_number_dfg, activities_q3, trace_len_q3), so results rely on pseudo-inverses and clamped eigenvalues.

n_events, epa_sequence_entropy, epa_sequence_entropy_exponential_forgetting and average_edit_distance reach the communality bound, indicating a possible Heywood case that makes Factor 2 less trustworthy.
Measure definitions only state the group, so interpretations rely on measure names and group descriptions.
Fifteen factors from an eigenvalue-based suggestion is probably more than the data support, since many factors explain under 2% of the variance each.
Many measures cross-load on Factors 1, 2 and 3, so these dimensions are not cleanly separated under varimax.
Factors reflect variance shared in this particular collection of 2112 logs and may change with other data, rotation or factor count.
